defects.guard_boundary: artifact-validator conformance to canonical protocol without false-positive merge blockers
defects.guard: artifact guards bind checks to the canonical semantic scope, accept equivalent valid formatting, and preserve escaped Markdown delimiters such as \| inside table cells; the architecture-readiness (ADPR) validator is scoped by the artifact's own canonical readiness claim rather than by repository path, because ARCHITECTURE_AUDIT_PROTOCOL.md limits its applicability to ADPR/readiness review and assigns implementation review to AI_REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md; the predicate is a disjunction over independent canonical readiness instruments (Governing protocol declaration, Final Verdict / Findings Matrix / Verdict Derivation headings, canonical verdict, canonical A-D finding record) so deleting one discriminator cannot evade validation, while non-readiness governed artifacts still receive protocol-independent baseline integrity validation; readiness classification recognizes a canonical verdict *declaration* parsed by the same _selected_verdicts() semantics the validator uses, never a bare verdict token, so an incidental, quoted, historical or negated mention cannot pull an AI_REVIEW_PROTOCOL implementation review into the ADPR readiness template while the remaining independent signals keep classification fail-safe

defects.guard_boundary: single rendered-Markdown structure boundary: CommonMark HTML block state including paragraph continuation, fences, indented code, and one shared ATX heading identity parser
defects.guard: semantic audit parsing runs on rendered structure only: all seven CommonMark HTML block types are masked, including block-level containers such as div/section/table, processing instructions, declarations and CDATA, alongside the earlier pre/script/style/textarea literals and HTML comments, while type 7 may not interrupt a paragraph so inline HTML in rendered prose is preserved; the same boundary recognizes ATX headings with CommonMark's legal 0-3 space indentation and rejects 4-space indented code, so neither literal content impersonating structure nor canonically valid equivalent indentation is mishandled; HTML block state tracks real paragraph continuation rather than a preceding-blank-line proxy, so a type 7 block correctly begins wherever the parser is between blocks -- after a heading, fence, or thematic break as well as after a blank line -- while still never interrupting an active paragraph; and one _parse_atx_heading() normalizer gives every heading consumer the same identity, accepting CommonMark's optional closing hash sequence as decoration while leaving unseparated trailing hashes such as '## Metadata###' as heading content

defects.guard: mandatory real headings cannot be empty where substantive scope/evidence/results/derivation/completion are required, Reviewed artifact identity is mandatory, and unresolved PENDING placeholders are rejected; the Audit Completion Check must record completed work rather than merely non-empty text: every rendered checklist item must be checked and the canonical template checklist topics must be covered, matched by topic so equivalent wording is accepted while a fabricated single item cannot impersonate the contract, scoped to that section so unchecked boxes elsewhere raise no false positive; completion topics are matched injectively against distinct rendered checked entries rather than against one concatenated body, so a single fabricated entry listing every topic keyword cannot stand in for the canonical item-by-item contract; a maximum bipartite matching is used so an entry able to satisfy several topics is never claimed by the wrong one and a canonically valid checklist is not falsely rejected; a checked entry must assert the required state rather than merely naming the topic: an entry that explicitly admits the work was not done cannot satisfy the item it contradicts, and the one canonical prohibition -- that the auditor did not recommend or rank options -- must positively assert absence, so a positive recommendation admission fails it; the guards are bound to completion verbs and to that prohibition rather than to bare negative words, so valid phrasings such as 'none omitted' are not falsely rejected

defects.guard_boundary: architecture-audit verdict section identity plus verdict, severity, and blocking semantics
defects.guard: one canonical verdict is derived bidirectionally from unresolved severity: A permits ready/minor, B rejects READY_FOR_ADR and permits minor/conditional, C requires ADPR_REVISION_REQUIRED, D requires ARCHITECTURE_NOT_READY; verdict section identity is counted independently of section content, so exactly one rendered level-two Final Verdict section may exist and a second identical or conflicting section cannot be ignored by section parsing that stops at the next heading; duplicate-looking verdict headings inside fenced, indented, commented, or raw-HTML literal regions do not count; verdict derivation stays bidirectional when the Findings Matrix has zero data rows, so a header-only matrix cannot reach an early return: per the protocol's Verdicts section READY_FOR_ADR_WITH_MINOR_FINDINGS requires at least one Class A or B finding and CONDITIONAL_ADR_READY requires cumulative Class B findings, leaving the no-finding case to READY_FOR_ADR

defects.guard: finding records use canonical Severity A-D and the matrix uses Class; validation is scoped to actual finding records so unrelated Severity prose cannot create a false-positive blocker; each canonical field may appear exactly once per rendered finding record, validated on an ordered field sequence before any normalized mapping exists, so a duplicate label -- contradictory, identical, or differing only by case -- cannot overwrite an earlier value and erase the state the record actually renders; matrix agreement is evaluated only after field cardinality is proven

defects.source: PR #293 Codex P1 reviews on 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-21; PR #293 Codex truncated-matrix-row recurrence on 2026-08-21; PR #293 Codex unrendered-matrix recurrence on 2026-08-21; PR #293 Codex duplicate-matrix-section recurrence on 2026-08-21
defects.guard_boundary: strict one-to-one architecture-audit finding record and matrix cross-validation
defects.guard: finding records and Findings Matrix rows are bidirectionally one-to-one by stable Finding ID: every rendered canonical record appears exactly once in the matrix and every matrix row maps to exactly one complete rendered record; duplicate record headings and duplicate matrix rows are rejected on cardinality rather than collapsed by a dict or set, so a rendered blocker cannot be omitted from the matrix and hidden from verdict derivation; record Severity and Blocks ADR must agree with the matrix; every candidate data row beneath a recognized Findings Matrix header is either parsed or reported, never silently skipped: a row with fewer cells than the header, or with no Finding identifier, is a deterministic error rather than a discarded row, so a truncated blocker cannot vanish from cardinality, severity, and verdict derivation at once, while blank template placeholder rows and separator rows remain non-data and escaped pipes remain cell content; the Findings Matrix counts only when it actually renders as a Markdown table: the canonical header must be immediately followed by a matching delimiter row, data rows are the contiguous table rows after it, and parsing stops where the rendered table ends, so pipe-prefixed prose, a delimiter placed later in the section, and an unrelated table elsewhere can neither establish nor rescue the mandatory matrix; the audit must contain exactly one rendered level-two Findings Matrix section, counted through the same heading-identity machinery as Final Verdict, so a second rendered matrix cannot hold an unresolved blocker that section-scoped reads never observe, while duplicate matrix headings inside fenced, commented, raw-HTML, or indented-code regions stay non-semantic
